fields.name: x
fields.description: Your x as the client sees it. The server uses it only for the grid check and for `correction`. It does not set your position from it.

fields.name: y
fields.description: Your y as the client sees it.

fields.name: going_x
fields.coerce: `parseFloat(going_x) || 0`, so a value that is not a number moves you toward x = 0

fields.name: m
fields.coerce: compared with `==` to `player.m`, so `"3"` also matches 3
fields.description: The map-change counter `m` from your last `player`, `start` or `new_map`. If it does not match, the server ignores the move.

fields.name: pet
fields.description: Move `player.monster` (your pet) instead of the character. Nothing sets `player.monster` (the `pet` handler always throws), so a move with `pet` does nothing.

fields.name: key
fields.coerce: the server pushes `key[0]`; a value that is not a string pushes `undefined`
fields.description: One konami key (`"u"`, `"d"`, `"l"`, `"r"`). The server adds it to `player.konami` while that list has fewer than 20 entries. It does this before the other checks, so also for a move that the server ignores. [`interaction`](#send-interaction) uses the list.

responses.name: Correction
responses.when: The move starts, your `x`, `y` is more than 132 px from your position on the server, and the grid cell at `x`, `y` has the value 0. `mode.enforce_smap` and `mode.lcorrection` must be on; both are on (node/server.js:278-279).

responses.name: Channels stopped
responses.when: The move starts and it removed one or more channels in `c` whose condition does not have `can_move` (for example fishing or mining). A normal move sends no `player`.
responses.summary: Your state without those channels in `c`.

failures.intro: A move that the server ignores sends nothing. Only the rows below send something.

rows.when: No character, and no `pet` and no `key`.

**Server bug:** the handler throws. With no character and `pet` set, it reads `player.monster` of `undefined`. With `key` set and no character, or `pet` set (nothing sets `player.monster`), it reads `konami` of `undefined`.

replies.note: from the socket wrapper, with 16 call-cost

rows.when: `m` does not match, you cannot walk (`can_walk`: disabled, or `dash` is active), or the destination is your position on the server now.

The grid cell at `x`, `y` or at the destination is unknown or not walkable (`smap` value 2 or more). The check is on the two points, not on the line between them. The server adds 1 to `player.violations` (`defeat_player`, node/server.js:4499-4524; in a cave run it kills you) and sends you to `jail`.

example.message: Make sure you only move with the built-in move function

replies.note: then `player`, from `transport_player_to(player, "jail")`: no effect, and no `direction` (the one `jail` spawn, design/maps.js, has none)

also.when: The move starts. The server marks you as changed (`u`), and the next entity update carries your new `going_x`, `going_y` and `move_num`.
also.summary: Your entity, with `moving: true`. Not while your instance is frozen (`start_moving_element` returns at once).

confirm.note: `u` puts you in the next `entities` of each client that sees you

order: nothing at once in most cases
`correction` to you, if your `x`, `y` is too far from the server position
`player` to you, if the move stopped a channel
later, `entities` to clients nearby with your movement
